text_to_speech: i serve as the director for eui japan i support gender diversity in the marketplace we help athletes think about their second career after they retire in sports i do recommend the three e's of experience exposure and education to really progress in your career hands-on experience is really really critical i mean you really don't understand it until you do it surround yourself with that network of mentors or advisors that from the exposure standpoint was really important and then third training find your strengths don't focus on your weaknesses so much acknowledge them but i think if you can focus on what you're good at the sky's the limit

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I serve as the director for EY Japan.
I support gender diversity in the marketplace.
We help athletes think about their second career after they retire in sports.
I do recommend the three ease of experience,
exposure and education to really progress in your career.
Hands-on experience is really, really critical.
I mean, you really don't understand it until you do it.
Surround yourself with that network of mentors or advisors.
That, from the exposure standpoint, was really important.
And then third training, find your strengths.
Don't focus on your weaknesses so much.
But I think if you can focus on what you're good at, the sky's a limit.

youtube_description:
Watch Janelle Sasaki, executive director of Diversity & Inclusion Services at Ernst & Young Advisory Co., Ltd. (EYA) in Tokyo, Japan. She advises on Diversity & Inclusion(D&I) practices in the workplace for Japan and the Asian Pacific Region. Watch her full interview at https://www.careergirls.org/role-model/diversity-inclusion-director-janelle-sasaki/.
